reasons.rubric: Roster-membership is a simple yes/no with a real employer issuer and revocation, but the building often needs the worker's name for accountability and employers rarely run credential issuance.
reasons.validity: Gate logbooks with ID numbers are a real Taiwan practice, but the predicate is insufficient if guards must record who entered, and employers are unlikely to issue short-lived signed credentials.
reasons.coherence: The idea itself admits that the verifier's accountability need conflicts with the unlinkable design, so the parts only partly fit.
reasons.novelty: Contractor on-site access is not touched by any known case and uses a new issuer (employer roster).
reasons.retention_law: Building logbooks are a management choice rather than a clearly mandated record, though security rules may require identifying visitors.
reasons.linkability: Revocation checks and per-visit presentation can be made unlinkable, but accountability wants linkability to a named person.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Small cleaning and security contractors have little incentive or tooling to run a revocable credential service.
reasons.no_wallet: Gate guards and workers would need wallets and readers, which is a heavy burden for a low-wage, high-turnover workforce.

reasons.rubric: The predicate is a date-window attestation with a hospital issuer and many students per year, but hospitals do not issue digital attestations and some cases legally need the diagnosis.
reasons.validity: Schools asking for diagnosis certificates over LINE is plausible, and a fitness-for-dates statement is mostly sufficient, though a hospital would have to sign a new kind of document.
reasons.coherence: Predicate, verifier, and issuer fit well, and the stated limits for infectious-disease cases are honest.
reasons.novelty: Health-related school absence is not on the known list and the attestation type is new.
reasons.provenance: The minimum-necessary framing and the yes/no proof pattern are described in generic terms and the idea would read nearly the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: Schools may have rules requiring the diagnosis for some conditions, and I cannot say whether they must retain it.
reasons.linkability: The proof is shown to one school for one window, so linkage across verifiers is low.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals have little reason to build a signing system for a low-value certificate, and physician liability makes them cautious.
reasons.no_wallet: Parents and young students would need a wallet, while a PDF over LINE is the easy path.

reasons.rubric: The predicate is a count over a ledger with a bank issuer and a verifier that over-collects, but it is a single-source multi-condition derived value and the landlord's decision rests on deposits and guarantors.
reasons.validity: Landlords asking for passbook pages is plausible, but a one-bank count is easily gamed by the tenant, cash rent is invisible, and banks would have to sign a new computed attestation.
reasons.coherence: The pieces fit, and the idea admits that the tenant picks the account, which weakens the proof.
reasons.novelty: Rent payment history is adjacent to the known renting case but uses a different issuer (bank) and predicate.
reasons.provenance: Both borrowings, limiting release to the purpose and stripping identifying fields, restate what any derived-count proof does and are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: Landlords have no apparent duty to keep full statements, so the retention law test does not block it.
reasons.linkability: A one-off signed count shown to a landlord carries little linkability risk.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Banks have little commercial reason to sign custom payment-regularity attestations for tenants.
reasons.no_wallet: Tenants and small landlords would need new tooling, whereas a screenshot works today.

reasons.rubric: Membership plus a single-use token is a clean predicate with a utility issuer, but the issuer ecosystem is narrow, frequency is low, and winners must give an address anyway.
reasons.validity: Rebate draws exist, but the stated Taipower roll and bill uploads are speculative and the proof protects only the entry stage.
reasons.coherence: Eligibility plus a nullifier fits an anonymous draw, and the limits are stated.
reasons.novelty: It touches the utility subsidy case but with a draw and de-duplication framing, so it is mostly a variation.
reasons.provenance: The separate-eligibility and single-use-token borrowings are both real mechanisms in the design, so they are faithful.
reasons.retention_law: I cannot tell whether the city must retain applicant records for a subsidy, and an audit duty is plausible.
reasons.linkability: Single-use tokens give de-duplication without tracking, which suits this design.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Taipower is a state-owned company that could sign rolls, but it has no obvious reason to build this for a small program.
reasons.no_wallet: Entrants would need a wallet to enter a small draw, while a bill photo upload is trivial.

reasons.rubric: A cross-issuer same-holder match is a complex multi-source predicate, frequency is very low, and consent files legally need identification anyway.
reasons.validity: A paid study needing both a university and hospital claim is contrived, the IRB likely wants identification, and a hospital issuer of an eligibility claim is implausible.
reasons.coherence: The idea gives its own weakness, that consent signatures need a real name, which undercuts the benefit to only ID and insurance numbers.
reasons.novelty: Research recruiting with a two-issuer join is a moment no known case touches.
reasons.provenance: The identifier-removal checklist and the whole-card exposure borrowings are loose analogies, and the idea reads the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: Consent forms with a name and signature probably must be kept, which limits the benefit.
reasons.linkability: A join proof between two issuers needs a shared binding, and the study office might link it to the consent file.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Hospitals and the insurer are unlikely to cooperate with a research recruiting flow.
reasons.no_wallet: Participants would need a wallet and two credentials for a one-off study.

reasons.rubric: A rank threshold is a simple predicate, but there is no trusted issuer commitment, the stakes are low, and the zkTLS route is an unofficial proof of a publisher response.
reasons.validity: Smurf checks in community tournaments are real, but handing over credentials is not typical and publishers do not sign, so it rests on zkTLS fragility and Taiwan-specific need is thin.
reasons.coherence: The idea notes that the proof must be bound to the entry handle, and that binding is hard in the zkTLS design.
reasons.novelty: Gaming accounts are far from any known case.
reasons.provenance: The borrowings, a service log of interests and juror anonymity, have no connection to a rank proof and are decorative.
reasons.retention_law: No retention duty applies to an informal tournament organizer.
reasons.linkability: A zkTLS proof can be tied to the handle by design and shown once per entry.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: The publisher is not a willing issuer and may forbid session proofs in its terms.
reasons.no_wallet: Players would need zkTLS tooling, and organizers will just accept a screenshot or in-game spectator check.

reasons.rubric: A same-person match across two institution-controlled credentials is a multi-source predicate with low frequency, and the host already issues its own account.
reasons.validity: Reciprocal library access exists, but the host knows the visitor it registered, so a match proof adds little and the host's own lending log is its choice.
reasons.coherence: The idea concedes both credentials are institution-controlled, which removes the independent-issuer premise of a join proof.
reasons.novelty: University library and lab access is not on the known list.
reasons.provenance: The borrowing of a log that is not a readable record of interests is a real motivation, but the juror-anonymity borrowing is decorative.
reasons.retention_law: I cannot say whether libraries or labs must keep lending records, though the host may need an equipment-use log.
reasons.linkability: Borrowing records can be unlinked from the national ID, but the host's own visitor account keeps them linkable across visits.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Universities that already trust each other can sign membership easily, but they have little reason to adopt new credentials.
reasons.no_wallet: Students would need a wallet for an occasional visit, and a student card and visitor form already work.

reasons.rubric: Current employment of a signer is a simple status predicate with an employer issuer and revocation, but frequency is low and tender rules require identified signers and auditable files.
reasons.validity: The company seal and authorisation letter are real tender practice, but verifiers want a named signer and a seal, so a proof only replaces ID copies and labor insurance records.
reasons.coherence: Freshness at the opening date and revocation fit well, and the limit on anonymity is stated.
reasons.novelty: Procurement is not on the known list, and the employer-authority claim is a new issuer and predicate, though it resembles the job and licence cases.
reasons.provenance: The sealed-bid timing and identity-document borrowings loosely describe the setting, and the idea would read the same without them.
reasons.retention_law: A bid file must be auditable and likely kept, which limits the benefit.
reasons.linkability: The signer is identified by design, so unlinkability is not wanted and is not at stake.
reasons.issuer_unwilling: Companies already issue seal letters and might issue a status credential, but they lack any current system for it.
reasons.no_wallet: Bidders would need wallets and the procurement system would need to verify them, whereas the paper seal is fully accepted.
